reuse.why: All changed consumers use getScheduledAmount, which also reuses the existing getApproxNumberThreshold tolerance helper.

duplication.why: The change removes repeated amount dispatch and midpoint calculations without introducing duplicate decision logic.

placement.why: Expected-amount policy remains in shared schedule logic, while API serialization and output typing remain in their established layers.

scope.why: The edits focus on the requested amount rules, their consumers, the API field, and associated tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: Centralized policy simplifies future changes, although the new test fixture unnecessarily bypasses type checking with double assertions.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Changed planning, posting, preview, display, and API consumers delegate to getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: Previously duplicated calculations are replaced with shared calls rather than renamed or reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains the op parameter and an isapprox conditional; both express required domain variation, and no changed consumer bypasses the helper.
